fields.label: Effect on an ionic nucleophile
fields.answer: Usually slower than in polar aprotic solvent: poor salt dissolution and tight ion pairing reduce free nucleophile.
options: Usually slower than in polar aprotic solvent: poor salt dissolution and tight ion pairing reduce free nucleophile.
Always faster because there are no O–H bonds.
The solvent changes an anion into a carbocation.
fields.explanation: Low polarity makes separated ions costly. This can reduce the available anion even without hydrogen-bond donation.

fields.label: Reason for similar SN1 rates
fields.answer: Both ionize to the same delocalized allylic cation, CH2=CH–CH+–CH3 ↔ +CH2–CH=CH–CH3.
options: Both ionize to the same delocalized allylic cation, CH2=CH–CH+–CH3 ↔ +CH2–CH=CH–CH3.
Every primary bromide ionizes as fast as every secondary bromide.
Both react by obligatory one-step backside substitution.
fields.explanation: The two drawings place the leaving group at opposite ends of one allylic system, so their ionization products share the same resonance stabilization.

fields.label: Ionization and resonance
fields.answer: Lose diphosphate from C3; shift the C1=C2 π pair to C2=C3 to place the positive charge at C1.
options: Lose diphosphate from C3; shift the C1=C2 π pair to C2=C3 to place the positive charge at C1.
fields.explanation: C–O bond electrons depart with diphosphate, forming an allylic cation.

fields.label: Ring-forming step
fields.answer: The C6=C7 π bond forms C6–C1, making a six-membered ring and placing the charge at C7.
options: The C6=C7 π bond forms C6–C1, making a six-membered ring and placing the charge at C7.
C7 bonds to C1 to form the requested six-membered ring.
The base forms the ring by bonding to C3.
fields.explanation: The C1–C6 path contains six carbons; joining its ends gives the limonene ring.

fields.label: Final step
fields.answer: A base removes H from a methyl attached to C7; its C–H pair forms the exocyclic C7=CH2 bond.
options: A base removes H from a methyl attached to C7; its C–H pair forms the exocyclic C7=CH2 bond.
Water adds to C7 to make limonene.
fields.explanation: Deprotonation of the tertiary carbocation creates limonene’s isopropenyl group.

fields.label: a · NaSCH3
fields.explanation: The two-carbon primary chloride undergoes SN2 with sulfur.

fields.label: a · NaOH
fields.explanation: Primary carbon allows direct replacement by OH.

fields.label: b · NaSCH3 · chapter elimination prediction
fields.selectionPrompt: If elimination follows the chapter’s qualitative prediction for this tertiary halide, which alkene products result?
fields.explanation: The shown substrate is tertiary 2-chloro-2-methylbutane. The two possible beta-H removals give these alkenes; this identifies the elimination products without claiming that methanethiolate must give only E2 under every condition.

fields.label: b · NaOH
fields.explanation: Strong base favors elimination at tertiary carbon; removing ethyl-side H gives the more substituted alkene.

fields.label: c · NaSCH3
fields.explanation: The soft, weakly basic sulfur nucleophile substitutes at the secondary ring carbon.

fields.label: c · NaOH
fields.explanation: For a secondary halide, hydroxide can act as both base and nucleophile.

fields.label: b · NaSCH3 · prediction limit
fields.selectionPrompt: Can the actual reaction pathway with methanethiolate be uniquely fixed without solvent and temperature?
fields.answer: No. Methanethiolate is a strong nucleophile but a relatively weak base; ionizing conditions can allow a substitution product, (CH3)2C(SCH3)CH2CH3, as well as competing elimination.
options: No. Methanethiolate is a strong nucleophile but a relatively weak base; ionizing conditions can allow a substitution product, (CH3)2C(SCH3)CH2CH3, as well as competing elimination.
Yes. Every sulfur nucleophile necessarily gives exclusive E2 at every tertiary halide.
Yes. Tertiary substrates always undergo fast SN2 with methanethiolate.
fields.explanation: Substrate structure blocks ordinary SN2, but it does not by itself choose between ionization/capture and base-induced elimination. The omitted medium and temperature affect that competition.

organic-11-21.coverage: Checks the specified products, configurations and mechanism choices; freehand drawing is not automatically assessed.
organic-11-21.reviewNotes: For (b), the textbook’s author manual predicts the two alkenes for both reagents. Methanethiolate is relatively weakly basic, however, and no solvent or temperature is specified; the checks distinguish those possible elimination products from an unsupported claim of a unique experimental pathway. The actual tertiary substrate has five carbons.

fields.label: Bromide precursor
fields.explanation: The carbon bearing acetate in the product is R, while the neighboring carbon stays S. Reverse only the substituted center to obtain the bromide.

fields.label: Reaction and product
fields.answer: Acetate displaces Br at C2, giving (2R,3S)-3-cyclohexylbutan-2-yl acetate.
options: Acetate displaces Br at C2, giving (2R,3S)-3-cyclohexylbutan-2-yl acetate.
Both centers invert to give the RR acetate.
fields.explanation: An SN2 event changes only the attacked stereocenter; the adjacent carbon retains its bonds and geometry.

fields.label: a · product
fields.explanation: Br− attacks the terminal carbon and expels tosylate.

fields.label: a · electron flow
fields.answer: Br lone pair → carbon bearing OTos; C–O bond → tosylate oxygen, in one step.
options: Br lone pair → carbon bearing OTos; C–O bond → tosylate oxygen, in one step.
C–O cleavage first forms a primary free carbocation.
Remove β-H first, then add Br.
fields.explanation: This is a concerted SN2 displacement.

fields.label: b · product
fields.explanation: The acetylide carbon connects to the primary bromide carbon, extending the skeleton by three carbons.

fields.label: b · electron flow
fields.answer: Acetylide carbon lone pair → CH2Br; C–Br pair → Br.
options: Acetylide carbon lone pair → CH2Br; C–Br pair → Br.
Attack the terminal methyl carbon and remove H−.
Attack the internal alkyne carbon with bromide.
fields.explanation: Primary backside attack makes a C–C bond.

fields.label: c · product
fields.explanation: The cyanide carbon replaces I on the exocyclic CH2 group.

fields.label: c · electron flow
fields.answer: Cyanide carbon lone pair → CH2I; C–I pair → I.
options: Cyanide carbon lone pair → CH2I; C–I pair → I.
I− adds to the ring first.
The cyclohexyl ring opens before substitution.
fields.explanation: The electrophile is primary even though it is attached to a ring.

fields.label: d · product stereochemistry
fields.answer: 3-(Methylthio)tetrahydrofuran with SCH3 dashed and H wedged at the original Cl center.
options: 3-(Methylthio)tetrahydrofuran with SCH3 dashed and H wedged at the original Cl center.
The same product with SCH3 wedged and H dashed.
fields.explanation: The original solid-wedge C–Cl is replaced with inverted C–S geometry.

fields.label: d · electron flow
fields.answer: S lone pair → carbon bearing Cl from the back; C–Cl pair → Cl.
options: S lone pair → carbon bearing Cl from the back; C–Cl pair → Cl.
Cl departs to a primary cation before sulfur approaches.
fields.explanation: Thiolate is a strong nucleophile and a relatively weak base.

fields.label: Common mechanism and reason
fields.answer: All are SN2: accessible primary/secondary electrophiles and strong nucleophiles favor concerted backside displacement.
options: All are SN2: accessible primary/secondary electrophiles and strong nucleophiles favor concerted backside displacement.
All are SN1 because solvent is aprotic.
All are E1cB because a leaving group is present.
fields.explanation: No carbonyl-stabilized anion or freely generated carbocation is required.

organic-11-25.coverage: Checks the specified products, configurations and mechanism choices; freehand drawing is not automatically assessed.

fields.label: a · sequence
fields.answer: Protonate OH; water leaves to give (CH3)2C+CH2CH3; Cl− captures the cation.
options: Protonate OH; water leaves to give (CH3)2C+CH2CH3; Cl− captures the cation.
Cl− attacks tertiary carbon in one step without activation.
OH− leaves first in neutral water.
fields.explanation: Protonation creates a good leaving group, and the tertiary cation is accessible.

fields.label: b · sequence
fields.answer: C–Cl ionization gives CH2=CH–CH+–CH3 ↔ +CH2–CH=CH–CH3; acetate capture at the original carbon gives the shown acetate.
options: C–Cl ionization gives CH2=CH–CH+–CH3 ↔ +CH2–CH=CH–CH3; acetate capture at the original carbon gives the shown acetate.
Acetate removes a vinylic H to produce the shown ester.
A primary nonallylic cation is required.
fields.explanation: Allylic delocalization lowers the cost of ionization.

fields.label: c · sequence
fields.answer: Br− leaves from C6H11CH2CH(Br)CH3; methanol attacks that cation; deprotonation gives C6H11CH2CH(OCH3)CH3.
options: Br− leaves from C6H11CH2CH(Br)CH3; methanol attacks that cation; deprotonation gives C6H11CH2CH(OCH3)CH3.
Methoxide is present at high concentration and guarantees SN2.
Methanol breaks a cyclohexane C–C bond.
fields.explanation: A weak neutral nucleophile in protic solvent supports the indicated ionization/capture pathway.

fields.label: Common mechanism
fields.answer: SN1: leaving-group loss precedes nucleophile capture.
options: SN1: leaving-group loss precedes nucleophile capture.
SN2: all bonds change in one step.
fields.explanation: The displayed substitutions pass through carbocations rather than requiring simultaneous backside attack.

fields.label: a · alkene set
fields.explanation: Protonation and water loss yield a tertiary cation, then removal of either type of β-H gives an alkene.

fields.label: b · product
fields.explanation: Chloride loss produces the allylic cation; loss of a terminal methyl H forms the conjugated diene.

fields.label: c · alkene set
fields.explanation: After water leaves C1, β-H can be lost from C2, C6 or the C1 methyl. The C1=C2 product is tetrasubstituted.

fields.label: Common mechanism and arrows
fields.answer: E1: activate OH if present, move the leaving-group bond pair onto the leaving group, then transfer a β C–H pair into C=C as base takes H.
options: E1: activate OH if present, move the leaving-group bond pair onto the leaving group, then transfer a β C–H pair into C=C as base takes H.
E2: the base must remove H before any leaving group can depart.
SN2: nucleophile replaces the leaving group with no alkene.
fields.explanation: The conditions permit a carbocation before deprotonation; anti geometry is not the defining requirement.

organic-11-27.coverage: Checks the specified products, configurations and mechanism choices; freehand drawing is not automatically assessed.

fields.label: a · product
fields.explanation: In the reactive diaxial chair of the trans substrate, the methyl-bearing neighbor has axial methyl instead of axial H; elimination occurs toward the other neighbor.

fields.label: b · product
fields.explanation: Bulky tert-butoxide removes the single β-H type while bromide leaves.

fields.label: c · product
fields.explanation: The quaternary β-carbon has no H, so elimination must use the methyl on the opposite side.

fields.label: Common mechanism and electron flow
fields.answer: E2: base → β-H, C–H → C=C, and C–leaving-group → leaving group, together in an anti arrangement.
options: E2: base → β-H, C–H → C=C, and C–leaving-group → leaving group, together in an anti arrangement.
E1: a carbocation must form first in every case.
E1cB: a carbonyl enolate is formed in every case.
fields.explanation: Strong base drives a concerted elimination; available β-H and geometry control the product.

fields.label: a · product
fields.explanation: Loss of the β-OH and an α-H creates a conjugated enone.

fields.label: b · product
fields.explanation: The new alkene joins the carbonyl-adjacent carbon to the carbon that carried OH.

fields.label: c · product
fields.explanation: The aldehyde-stabilized anion eliminates the adjacent hydroxide.

fields.label: Common sequence
fields.answer: E1cB: base removes an α-H; the resonance-stabilized anion forms C=C while the β C–O pair leaves with OH−.
options: E1cB: base removes an α-H; the resonance-stabilized anion forms C=C while the β C–O pair leaves with OH−.
OH− leaves first to give a free β-carbocation.
Base attacks the carbonyl and removes the entire alkyl chain.
fields.explanation: Carbonyl stabilization makes deprotonation feasible before loss of the poor leaving group.

fields.label: a · product and mechanism
fields.explanation: An enolate at the carbonyl-adjacent ring carbon expels the neighboring hydroxide.

fields.label: b · product and mechanism
fields.explanation: Phenoxide attacks the primary ethyl iodide carbon.

fields.label: c · product and mechanism
fields.explanation: Tertiary iodide ionizes in methanol; capture at either face and deprotonation forms the ether.

fields.label: d · product and mechanism
fields.explanation: Ethoxide promotes elimination; loss of ethyl-side β-H forms the less strained exocyclic alkene rather than a cyclopropene double bond.

organic-11-30.reviewNotes: Product predictions refer to the principal textbook pathways; minor competing elimination products are not assigned a fixed ratio.

fields.label: First electron-pair movement
fields.answer: OH− removes the alcohol proton; the O–H bond pair stays on the substrate oxygen to make an alkoxide.
options: OH− removes the alcohol proton; the O–H bond pair stays on the substrate oxygen to make an alkoxide.
OH− attacks bromine to make BrOH.
The C–C bond breaks to make two carbocations.
fields.explanation: The substrate’s own oxygen becomes the nucleophile.

fields.label: Ring closure
fields.answer: The alkoxide lone pair attacks the adjacent C–Br carbon from the back while the C–Br pair leaves with Br−.
options: The alkoxide lone pair attacks the adjacent C–Br carbon from the back while the C–Br pair leaves with Br−.
Oxygen attacks its own carbon and makes a two-membered ring.
Br− leaves first and OH attacks both faces.
fields.explanation: Intramolecular SN2 makes a three-membered epoxide with inversion only at the carbon that carried Br.

fields.label: Product stereochemistry
fields.answer: cis-2,3-Dimethyloxirane; the two methyl groups are on the same face.
options: cis-2,3-Dimethyloxirane; the two methyl groups are on the same face.
fields.explanation: The alcohol carbon retains its orientation while the neighboring center inverts.

organic-11-31.coverage: Checks the specified products, configurations and mechanism choices; freehand drawing is not automatically assessed.

fields.label: Why SN2 fails
fields.answer: The bridge framework blocks the required backside approach at the tertiary bridgehead.
options: The bridge framework blocks the required backside approach at the tertiary bridgehead.
Bromide is always a poor leaving group.
The molecule contains no C–Br bond.
fields.explanation: The attacking trajectory would pass into the cage.

fields.label: Why ordinary SN1 fails
fields.answer: The small bridged skeleton cannot readily flatten the bridgehead into a normal trigonal carbocation.
options: The small bridged skeleton cannot readily flatten the bridgehead into a normal trigonal carbocation.
A bridgehead cation is automatically more stable than benzyl.
SN1 requires a strong nucleophile before ionization.
fields.explanation: Ionization would demand a severe geometric distortion at the constrained bridgehead.

organic-11-32.coverage: Checks all requested objective outcomes and reasoning choices.

fields.label: Mechanism class
fields.explanation: Oxidation has placed a carbonyl next to the ring carbon bearing the sulfur-containing side chain.

fields.label: Electron flow and departing group
fields.answer: Base removes the ring α-H; the enolate forms the exocyclic C=C while the C–S pair goes to sulfur; protonation releases homocysteine.
options: Base removes the ring α-H; the enolate forms the exocyclic C=C while the C–S pair goes to sulfur; protonation releases homocysteine.
The sulfur lone pair attacks adenine to open that ring.
Water leaves first to create an allylic carbocation.
fields.explanation: The new carbonyl stabilizes the intermediate anion, which expels the homocysteine thiolate.

organic-11-33.coverage: Checks the specified products, configurations and mechanism choices; freehand drawing is not automatically assessed.

fields.label: Major product Lewis structure
fields.answer: CH3CH2–C≡N: ; C and N are neutral, and N has one lone pair.
options: CH3CH2–C≡N: ; C and N are neutral, and N has one lone pair.
fields.explanation: Carbon attack by cyanide makes a nitrile; four bonds at nitrile carbon and three plus a lone pair at N give zero formal charges.

fields.label: Minor product Lewis structure
fields.answer: CH3CH2–N+≡C:− ; terminal C has one lone pair.
options: CH3CH2–N+≡C:− ; terminal C has one lone pair.
fields.explanation: Isonitrile nitrogen has four bonds (+1); terminal carbon has three bonds and one lone pair (−1).

fields.label: Two mechanisms
fields.answer: C-end attack of CN− gives nitrile; N-end attack gives isonitrile. Both attack CH2I by SN2 while C–I breaks.
options: C-end attack of CN− gives nitrile; N-end attack gives isonitrile. Both attack CH2I by SN2 while C–I breaks.
Both products require first forming an ethyl carbocation.
The nitrile forms by attacking iodine rather than carbon.
fields.explanation: Cyanide is ambident: either end can form a bond to the electrophile, though carbon bonding predominates.

organic-11-34.coverage: Checks the specified products, configurations and mechanism choices; freehand drawing is not automatically assessed.

fields.label: Arginine connectivity
fields.explanation: Removing the succinate-derived substituent leaves the guanidinium side chain of arginine.

fields.label: Elimination mechanism
fields.answer: Base removes H from the succinate CH2; C–H electrons form the C=C and the adjacent C–N bond pair goes to N; proton transfer yields arginine and trans fumarate.
options: Base removes H from the succinate CH2; C–H electrons form the C=C and the adjacent C–N bond pair goes to N; proton transfer yields arginine and trans fumarate.
Water attacks the guanidinium carbon and removes ammonia only.
The substrate undergoes a methyl SN2 displacement.
fields.explanation: The eliminated N substituent and a β-H define the two atoms lost while the succinate carbons form fumarate.

organic-11-35.coverage: Checks the specified products, configurations and mechanism choices; freehand drawing is not automatically assessed.
organic-11-35.reviewNotes: This check describes the net base-catalyzed elimination arrows and proton transfers; it does not assert that the enzyme has a freely solvated carbocation.

fields.label: Proposed bond changes
fields.answer: I− attacks the ester methyl carbon by SN2; the methyl–O bond breaks to give CH3I and RCO2−.
options: I− attacks the ester methyl carbon by SN2; the methyl–O bond breaks to give CH3I and RCO2−.
I− attacks carbonyl carbon and ejects CH3−.
A free methyl cation forms before iodide attacks.
fields.explanation: Methyl carbon is accessible and carboxylate is a resonance-stabilized leaving group.

fields.label: Explain both observations
fields.answer: DMF leaves iodide more reactive than protic ethanol; an ethyl electrophile is more hindered than methyl.
options: DMF leaves iodide more reactive than protic ethanol; an ethyl electrophile is more hindered than methyl.
DMF supplies protons and ethyl is less hindered.
Both observations require a free methyl carbocation.
fields.explanation: The solvent and steric trends agree with backside substitution.

fields.label: Additional discriminating evidence
fields.answer: Measure first-order dependence on ester and iodide; a chiral alkyl ester should invert at the attacked carbon if it reacts by this route.
options: Measure first-order dependence on ester and iodide; a chiral alkyl ester should invert at the attacked carbon if it reacts by this route.
Test only whether the reaction vessel is glass.
Expect the rate to be independent of iodide and complete retention at the attacked center.
fields.explanation: Bimolecular kinetics and stereochemical inversion directly test an SN2 proposal.

fields.label: Neighboring-group step

fields.label: Why heating yields chloride
fields.answer: Tosylation first makes ROTos; chloride released from TosCl then attacks the primary carbon by SN2 and expels tosylate.
